ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and shareholders are screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's national counter-terrorism/AML list under Law 23 of 2015. PEP status, including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates, triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval. Negative-news and adverse-media checks are mandatory. Screening results and risk files are retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sede Electrónica (online portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be composed using the Latin alphabet. If the desired name is in a non-Latin script, it must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a Spanish translation. The statutory suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' is required. The Public Registry rejects names that are misleading, strikingly similar to an existing registered company, or contrary to public policy, applying phonetic and visual comparison standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the resident agent files a Recurso de Reconsideración with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five business days from notification, providing modified wording or arguments against the similarity/prohibition finding. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal (Recurso de Apelación) may be filed with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias within ten business days. To minimize delay, the applicant may simultaneously request a new name reservation using a distinctive alternative. A formal written decision is expected within twenty business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are permissible as administrative and commercial service addresses for a non-regulated online consignment business, provided the statutory resident agent maintains a physical office in Panama and the registered office on file with the Public Registry is the resident agent's physical address. A virtual office cannot replace the statutory resident agent or the registered office requirement. No storefront zoning license is required for this e-commerce activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection of the registered office in the first year is approximately 5% (low-to-medium). Risk may increase if the entity processes high transaction volumes, exhibits invoice mismatches, or engages in cash-based settlements. The resident agent is subject to AML supervision and may be audited at any time by the competent Panamanian supervisory authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas (Law 32 of 1927), as amended by Law 4 of 2015 and Law 5 of 2015; incorporation and corporate governance provisions at Arts. 1-8 (formation), Arts. 11-14 (capital), Art. 20 (registered office and resident agent), Arts. 34-43 (directors), and Arts. 44-50 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Section / Corporate Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation), registered through the Aviso de Constitución and evidenced by the Certificado de Inscripción
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under Law 32 of 1927. The share capital must be stated in the public deed and at least one share must be issued and subscribed; no escrow deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company validly subscribed to and accepted the initial share issuance as provided in the public incorporation deed of [date], allotting one or more ordinary no-par-value shares to each founding subscriber and recording such subscription in the shareholders’ register. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be at [Panamanian physical address] and the resident agent shall be the registered agent of record. FURTHER RESOLVED, that ______________ is appointed President, ______________ is appointed Treasurer, ______________ is appointed Secretary, and ______________ is appointed Compliance Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or successor appointment. All actions taken to implement these resolutions are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and obtain name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) via the online 'Panamá Emprende' module / 'Certificado de Nominación' window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names through the electronic nomination system. Pay the nomination fee and obtain the Certificado de Nominación, valid for 30 days. The name must include 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' and must not conflict with existing names. Deliver the certificate to the notary for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of the incorporator
Proof of payment of the nomination fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an electronic reconsideration ('recurso de reconsideración') within five business days, or submit amended alternatives. A second nomination fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and notarize public incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notario Público, appointed under the Judiciary / Corte Suprema de Justicia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators appear before a Panamanian notary and execute the Escritura Pública de Constitución, containing the articles of incorporation, corporate purpose for ISIC 4791, capital structure, registered office, directors, and officers. The notary verifies identity, reviews the name certificate, and incorporates the deed into notarial protocol. Notarization is mandatory before registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Passports or IDs of all incorporators
Draft corporate bylaws in Spanish or English with notarized Spanish translation if needed
Record of subscribed shares and subscriber details
Registered office address and resident agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect or missing consent, prepare and execute an amended deed. For translation deficiencies, obtain certified Spanish versions and re-notarize before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register incorporation deed with Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Sociedades (Corporate Registry Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarial protocol copy and certified copy to the Corporate Registry Section for mercantile inscription. Pay the statutory registry fees and document tax. After approval, the Registry issues the Certificado de Inscripción. The Aviso de Constitución must be published in a nationwide official medium and the proof of publication delivered to the Registry if required.
required_dossiers: Materialized notarized public deed (original and certified copy)
Identification of incorporators and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues preventive notes or precautionary observations, cure the requested documentation within the statutory term (generally 30 business days). For substantive inconsistencies, execute and register an amendment deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RUC, municipal operating notice, and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of the registered address for Aviso de Operación de Empresa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate RUC application using the Certificado de Inscripción and public deed. Obtain the corporate taxpayer identification number. Register the business with the local municipality using the Aviso de Operación form, indicating the e-commerce and consignment resale activity. No separate industrial license is required for ISIC 4791; any physical storage facility must comply with municipal use and sanitation rules.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the legal representative
Lease or ownership proof of the registered office
Proof of solvency or economic rights notification, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve DGI queries through the Telemáticos electronic portal or by attending the DGI service window. For municipal observations, correct zoning or padron data and pay any resulting local tax before issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Institute statutory corporate books and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent (abogado residente) and the Public Registry; notary for certified share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting approving the pro-forma resolutions, issue share certificates, and record subscriptions. Maintain the shareholders’ register, directors’ register, board minutes book, and share transfer register. Ensure the resident agent and legal representative acceptance documents are signed and retained at the registered office. If the company uses variable capital, register the variable capital declaration in accordance with Law 32 of 1927.
required_dossiers: Share subscription list and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate books are challenged or ultra vires acts are identified, retroactively legalize the books by notarial protocol submission or execute written shareholder consent to ratify actions and register corrected entries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 4791 online consignment and luxury resale is not an industrial manufacturing activity; no manufacturing or industrial establishment is operated.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación de Empresa (Business Operation Notice) issued under the Municipality Tax Law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Department of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category I (low-impact) for purely commercial e-commerce resale without physical storage; a Category I Environmental Impact Assessment may apply only if a bonded warehouse or significant physical logistics hub is opened.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or discharge thresholds apply to remote sales operations. If a physical warehouse is established, comply with MiAMBIENTE solid waste segregation obligations, municipal sanitation standards, and Ley 1 de 2005 (or successor waste regulations).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and structural/occupancy clearance from the local Municipality are required only when a physical office, warehouse, or storage area is used. Purely remote e-commerce operations may remain exempt until physical premises are established.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de la República de Panamá; online portal: E-Tax 2.0 (https://etax.mef.gob.pa) including the integrated SIFE electronic-invoicing module; customs counterpart for export control: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) de Panamá.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned S.A. procurement of the statutory RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente): (1) appoint a resident legal agent (abogado idóneo) and register the corporation at the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación where Panamanian-source commerce is carried on, or retain pure offshore status where all sales are consummated abroad; (3) apply via the E-Tax 2.0 portal by submitting the corporate registration certificate, the articles of incorporation, the resident agent's sworn appointment, and the Aviso de Operación; (4) upon RUC issuance, enroll in the ITBMS taxable-person ledger and request authorization to issue Digital Fiscal Receipts (SIFE electronic invoicing); (5) register with the ANA as an exporter (Código de Exportador) for physical shipments. Non-resident e-commerce suppliers may alternatively be registered through a Panamanian fiscal representative under the DGI digital-commerce registration channel.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in Panama. The monetary regime is full dollarization with the U.S. dollar as legal tender. Banking supervision and FX-services regulation are conducted by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Panama Superintendency of Banks), while Banco Nacional de Panamá operates as the state's fiscal agent and clearing bank without exercising central-bank powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains a fully dollarized monetary system without central-bank exchange controls. There is no regulatory distinction between capital-account and current-account convertibility for ordinary corporate transactions; shareholders' capital contributions, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, profit remittances, import settlements and export collections may all be freely converted and transferred in U.S. dollars or other acceptable currencies. The practical compliance hurdle is not convertibility but satisfying anti-money-laundering source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership documentation at the Panamanian bank and at the U.S. correspondent clearing bank. Profit remittance is structurally unrestricted under Panama's territorial tax system, provided the Dominican-entity profits arise from Panamanian-source activities and tax obligations, if any, are settled through the appropriate declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement that export receipts be brought through a specific clearing channel. Luxury resale export proceeds retained in U.S. dollars or in any freely convertible currency may be held offshore or repatriated without exchange-approval conditions. The only binding obligations are standard commercial record-keeping, availability of export documentation for banking and Superintendency-of-Banks review, and compliance with anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating and treasury concentration account; merchant settlement clearing account
Corporate operating account; capital escrow / settlement account for online resale
Corporate operating account with card-settlement integration for e-commerce platforms
Escrow-agent account and private-client settlement account for international trade
Operational account and trade-finance facility for documentary letter-of-credit disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a secondary collection and disbursement rail, but Low as the sole treasury liquidity hub. Panama has no separate digital-EMI licensing category; a non-bank payment institution operating without a licensed Panamanian banking or financial-services authorization cannot rely on direct ACH membership or on local clearing privileges. Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud and Wise Business may be used for cross-border card acquiring, FX conversion and vendor payouts, but the primary liquidity and settlement backbone must be a Tier-1 local bank account. Legal constraints include counterparty-concentration risk, the requirement that EMI balances be segregated, possible OFAC and Bank Secrecy Act review at U.S. correspondent banks, and the practical need for standardized SWIFT MT103 movement between the EMI rail and the Panamanian operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview is generally mandatory for a new Sociedad Anónima with foreign shareholders. At least one director or authorized signer with 25% or more UBO ownership is expected to appear before the bank's compliance officer or a Panamanian notary. The resident agent must be engaged, and the corporate charter and public-registry certificate must be legalized or apostilled. A remote-only opening is possible at the bank's discretion where the S.A. already has an established foreign banking reference and all UBO documentation is delivered via a licensed attorney, but enhanced due diligence will generally require a physical or videoconference interview with independent verification before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border resale of branded luxury goods with pricing inconsistent with the stated business profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company registration and techo; certified S.A. by-laws; CPA-reviewed or audited financial projections; purchase invoices from wholesale and consignment suppliers; authentication certificates for high-value lots; marketplace seller-agreement; and a 12-month transaction history demonstrating sustainable commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiaries and payees located in jurisdictions that do not match the physical movement of goods, or settlement routed through multiple payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Airway bills and Panama Customs e-sigla records; resale-platform payout reports; buyer KYC summaries; signed consignment contracts; a goods-flow diagram from acquisition to end customer; and a reconciliation schedule matching each inbound settlement to a specific sale or auction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs with politically exposed person status, high-risk nationality, or unexplained source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; proof of residential address; beneficial-ownership declaration and corporate-structure chart; sworn source-of-wealth statement prepared by counsel; PEP and sanctions screening reports; resident-agent certification; and a letter of reference from the UBO's existing licensed foreign bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receiving settlement from escrow or online auction platforms without clear buyer identity and with chargeback or fraud exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed escrow tri-party agreement; platform AML policy summary; bank statements proving card-linked or bank-origin inflows only; platform buyer and seller identity records; detailing of any buy-now/pay-later settlement logic; and standard customs or VAT declarations supporting each imported and exported luxury item.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire-transfer protocol: the shareholder must remit paid-in capital via SWIFT MT103 from a pre-existing account held in the shareholder's own name, using the beneficiary legal name of the Panamanian S.A., its exact bank account number, and the bank's SWIFT/BIC code. The payment memo should clearly read 'Aporte de capital / Capital contribution' or 'Share subscription — paid-in capital' and identify the S.A. tax identification reference. Verification requirements include a certified copy of the capital increase or subscription resolution, a source-of-funds certificate from the remitting bank, and confirmation that the wire originator matches the declared UBO or shareholder. Because Panama is dollarized and the U.S. correspondent bank will clear the transfer, OFAC screening and beneficial-ownership information must be available immediately; no Panamanian foreign-investment registration or exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: use SWIFT MT103 for supplier and consignment payouts, auction-house remittances, and ordinary vendor payments; use SWIFT MT202 for internal liquidity sweeps between the Tier-1 Panamanian bank and fintech EMI rails; use irrevocable documentary letters of credit under SWIFT MT700 for high-value purchases from European and North American auction houses; and use Panama's domestic ACH clearing for local fulfillment, logistics, and administrative payments. All outbound transactions settle directly in U.S. dollars with no FX approval, but the bank may require supporting invoices, customs declarations, and beneficiary KYC for transactions above its enhanced due-diligence threshold. Merchant settlement from Stripe and Escrow-Pay platforms is generally received through card-network payouts or SWIFT MT103 credits and should be reconciled against platform payout reports and buyer transaction logs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable spot and outright forward contracts for European sourcing exposure
USD/GBP deliverable forwards for United Kingdom auction-house purchases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in MXN, COP and BRL to hedge Latin-American collection proceeds into USD
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps under ISDA for EUR- or USD-denominated working-capital facilities
Vanilla USD/EUR foreign-exchange options and zero-cost collars for committed purchase orders
FX swaps combining spot and forward USD/EUR transactions for inventory-financing cash-flow matching

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax on Panamanian Legal Entities (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas) with DGI payment receipt confirming good standing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; the maintenance year follows the 1 January – 31 December calendar period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a statutory surcharge plus monthly accruing interest; non-payment for the period fixed by the Registro Público, generally three consecutive years, is a ground for administrative strike-off and dissolution; reinstatement requires payment of arrears, penalties and a registry restoration procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) for Panamanian-source income; not required for a wholly offshore S.A. with no local-source revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December; return due on or before 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file when obligated results in graduated monetary fines, monthly interest on any tax due, administrative closure of the RUC/tax identification number, and possible criminal tax-fraud liability for directors and officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Update / UBO Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiario Final, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / Dirección General de Ingresos, with data reflected in the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing before 30 June of each maintenance year in the standard schedule; any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership is additionally reportable within 30 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete or false UBO filings are subject to administrative fines imposed under Law 129 of 2020 and Executive Decree 16 of 2020; continued non-compliance suspends good-standing certificates and can impair registry filings, banking transactions and the annual franchise tax clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Renewal and Annual Compliance Certificate for the S.A.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent maintained under Law 32 of 1927
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewed simultaneously with the 30 June franchise tax payment; the resident agent confirms the current directors, officers, shareholders and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent is a statutory violation of the corporate law; the entity loses a valid service-of-process channel and may be struck off by the Registro Público at the request of the regulatory authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit applies to an ordinary private non-issuer S.A. Mandatory independent audit is triggered by regulated financial, insurance, trust or securities-issuer status, or by an express order of the DGI; lenders and licensed payment service providers may additionally require a CPA-reviewed or audited financial statement as a contractual matter.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS/NIIF as adopted by Panama for public-interest entities; NIIF para las PYMEs for small and medium enterprises; books may be kept in Spanish or English and must reflect the territorial-source tax basis applicable to Panamanian income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A. must keep a complete ownership chain at the resident agent's office. Within 30 business days of any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership, the updated UBO declaration must be filed with the Beneficial Owner Registry. Annually, the directors and UBOs must execute a written confirmation, signed under penalty of perjury, verifying that the recorded beneficial ownership is current; this confirmation is retained by the resident agent as part of the corporate record.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000 – US$8,000 per engagement; not required for the standard wholly offshore S.A.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions for ordinary S.A. taxpayers; wholly offshore-source income is excluded under territorial taxation. Optional preferential regimes may apply only if the taxpayer obtains dedicated licensing (e.g., SEM, Panama Pacifico, or free zone regimes).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1273 – Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically via DGI Panama (Dirección General de Ingresos) online platform 'DGI Empresas' with Spanish-language digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months following the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from Panama-source commercial activity, including consignment fees and markups from the resale of vintage luxury items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the S.A. is managed and effectively operated through non-resident owners without a Panama-sourced economic nexus, the company must treat revenue as Panama-source only when the sale, delivery, or business operation is attributable to Panama; otherwise enter zero and maintain detailed documentation of offshore activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_example: In a Panama-based online luxury resale operation, the full final sale price less consignor share is reportable as gross commission revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales returns, consignment clawbacks, chargebacks, and contractual discounts attributable to the reported Panama-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may reduce gross revenue only if the trade or business activity involving the returned goods took place in Panama or is directly linked to reported Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Post-sale escrow refunds triggered by buyer authentication disputes should be included here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Derived net gross revenue subject to Panamanian corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the net amount of Panama-source consignment sales only; exclude any passive investment income arising from foreign securities or bank accounts except when specifically sourced to Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Commission received from cross-border consignors whose goods never physically enter Panama may be treated as non-Panama-source if all commercial activity occurs offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net revenue less direct cost of goods sold, including costs of acquisition, authentication, restoration, and inbound logistics attributable to the Panama source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident S.A. must apportion these costs solely against Panama-source revenue; no deduction is allowed for expenses incurred in generating foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Costs of acquiring Hermès or Chanel items from Panamanian consignors are deductible against sales in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly and necessarily incurred in producing Panama-source taxable income, including warehouse rent, logistics, banking charges, escrow fees, insurance, and depreciation of equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners using a Panama administrator must keep an audited cost allocation if mixed local and foreign operations exist. Improper allocation triggers a full denial of the deduction for the related foreign income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Payment platform fees (Stripe) and escrow service charges are deductible if they relate to Panama sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Net Taxable Income (Line 4 minus Line 5)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting net taxable income derived exclusively from Panama-source operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee officers or trustees must avoid entering offshore capital gains or interest here; they are outside the territorial tax net.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Profit from a sale of a collectible handbag delivered into Panama is taxable, while a simultaneous cross-border ATO transaction between foreign parties is not.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward deduction of operating losses arising in prior fiscal years, limited to a maximum of five consecutive years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses that were computed against Panama-source income are eligible. Losses from offshore activity cannot be used to reduce the Panama-source tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: A loss incurred in a prior Panama-based vintage resale year may fully offset current-year Panama taxable income within the 5-year window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Corporation Tax Payable (25% of Line 6 adjusted)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% of net taxable income after NOL carryforwards and permitted credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the S.A. has neither assets nor activity in Panama and earns all income abroad, the annual return will show zero taxable income, but a minimum amount may still be due under the Alternative Minimum Tax regime based on net assets located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.example: Online luxury resale LLCs with Panama-only registration and no Panamanian office should declare zero if the digital marketplace operations are entirely foreign.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge is 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction thereof, up to 50% of the total tax due. In addition, a fixed fine of USD 10 to USD 500 may apply; interest at the Banco Nacional rate accrues at a minimum of 1.5% per month. Criminal tax evasion penalties can reach 2 to 5 times the tax omitted, and persistent nonfiling can trigger forced dissolution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid from Panamanian-source taxable profits, applicable to both resident and non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty dividend reduction, the beneficial owner must provide the Panamanian paying agent and DGI with: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty-state revenue authority, (ii) a certified legalized questionnaire or competent authority confirmation, and (iii) an executed physical or electronic form for reduced withholding under the relevant DTA. The payer must retain the documentation for five years. Panama maintains a limited DTA network (e.g., Korea, Singapore, Chile, Mexico, and several Caribbean states). Without a complete application before the distribution event, the 10% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate on royalties is 12.5% for use of trademarks, patents, and similar intangibles in Panama; treaty rates may reduce this to 5% in applicable DTAs. Interest paid to unrelated non-resident lenders is generally not subject to Panamanian withholding when it is not sourced to a commercial activity in Panama, but interest on Panamanian real‑secured loans and certain intra-group financing operations may become taxable. Under DTAs, interest ceilings commonly drop to 5% or 0% depending on agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.note_on_foreign_safe_harbor: A Panama S.A. that has received dividends from an entirely offshore operation may distribute those same funds without making reference to Panamanian active income; however, if a Panama-based luxury resale collects the sale proceeds, the revenue is ordinarily Panama-source and the 10% distribution withholding applies.
